papers.title: State and parameter estimation for a neural model of local field potentials.
papers.summary: The paper develops a Bayesian data assimilation approach using a discretized Wilson-Cowan-Armari neural field model to jointly estimate state and parameters from local field potential (LFP) measurements. It demonstrates feasibility on synthetic data and then applies it to mouse cortical LFP during natural sleep, showing that the method can characterize external forcing parameters while inferring a state consistent with the observed signal.

papers.title: Chronic cohabitation with CD1 male mice induces anxiety-like behaviors, reduced spontaneous alternation, dysregulated HPA axis, and disrupted sleep architecture in C57BL/6J female mice.
papers.summary: The study shows that 14-day co-housing of C57BL/6J female mice with CD1 male mice induces anxiety-like behaviors and cognitive deficits, alongside reduced serum estrogen, HPA axis dysregulation, and disrupted sleep architecture (reduced wakefulness, prolonged NREM and REM sleep). These changes were associated with decreased cell density in ventral hippocampal CA1 and CA3 and downregulated BDNF in those regions.

papers.title: Astrocyte-centered temporal resilience at the brain-behavior-immunity interface: sleep-circadian disruption and perioperative cognitive vulnerability in older adults.
papers.summary: This narrative review proposes an astrocyte-centered temporal resilience framework to integrate sleep-circadian disruption, neuroimmune signaling, and perioperative cognitive vulnerability in older adults. It synthesizes evidence on astrocytic clocks, inflammatory-metabolic stress, sleep fragmentation, circadian misalignment, and glymphatic physiology, but notes that direct evidence for an astrocyte-specific causal pathway in perioperative populations remains limited and the framework is hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: Theta-frequency subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation selectively improves visual attention in Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: In 39 Parkinson's disease patients with bilateral STN-DBS, theta-frequency (5 Hz) stimulation selectively improved visual attention accuracy in those with pre-existing attentional deficits (n=21), whereas high-frequency (130 Hz) stimulation reduced accuracy. These behavioral effects were paralleled by enhanced P300 amplitude under 5 Hz and suppressed P300 amplitude under 130 Hz, with no significant effects in the normal attention group.

papers.title: A subject-specific mechanistic model of affect links electroencephalography, cardiorespiratory feedback, and monoaminergic dynamics.
papers.summary: The paper presents a subject-specific computational framework linking EEG-derived cortical activity, cardiorespiratory dynamics, and putative monoaminergic processes to subjective affect. When evaluated on the AMIGOS dataset (9 participants, 16 video stimuli), the model reproduced participant-specific valence-arousal ratings during calibration, but leave-one-stimulus-out cross-validation showed more consistent prediction for arousal (RMSE 0.380) than for valence (RMSE 1.283), highlighting inter-individual variability and the need for larger validation.

papers.title: A wearable accelerometry landscape of human health and disease.
papers.summary: Analyzed a large-scale accelerometry cohort of 70,473 participants with up to 10 years of follow-up to construct an atlas of 210 accelerometer-derived phenotypes, identifying 8,149 ADP-disease and 36,614 ADP-trait associations across 406 diseases and 956 traits. Developed an AI framework (WATSNet) achieving AUC >0.7 for 112 incident and 65 prevalent diseases, and provided behavioral benchmarks (e.g., at least 0.8 h/day of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, 10,000 daily steps, 7.8 h sleep) associated with lower disease risks.

papers.title: Silibinin Alleviates Cognitive Dysfunction, Biochemical Alterations, and Hippocampal Structural Changes Induced by 5 days of Sleep Deprivation with or Without a Subsequent 24-H Recovery in Rats.
papers.summary: Investigated the effects of silibinin on cognitive dysfunction and hippocampal alterations induced by 5 days of sleep deprivation with or without 24-h recovery in rats, finding that silibinin significantly attenuated behavioral, biochemical, hormonal, histopathological, and immunohistochemical alterations, with further improvement after recovery sleep, restoring most parameters to control levels. Suggested that silibinin protects against sleep deprivation-induced cognitive dysfunction and hippocampal injury by reducing oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and neuroendocrine disturbances.

papers.title: TMS-Evoked Cortical Reactivity Signatures as a Multidimensional Biomarker of Depression: A TMS-EEG Meta-Analysis from Diagnosis to Prognosis.
papers.summary: Conducted a meta-analysis of 21 TMS-EEG studies (1,025 MDD patients, 517 healthy controls) to evaluate cortical reactivity signatures as multidimensional biomarkers for major depressive disorder, finding enhanced negative-polarity components in MDD (Hedges' g=0.36), particularly N100 (g=0.35), which was associated with symptom severity (g=0.67). Treatment attenuated N100 (g=-0.21) and elevated P180 (g=0.52), and treatment-induced reduction in negative-polarity responses was strongly coupled with clinical remission (g=0.91), with baseline negative-polarity components predicting treatment response (g=1.35).

papers.title: Resting-state frontal theta/beta ratio and psychological symptoms in college students: an EEG study.
papers.summary: Recorded resting-state EEG from 222 undergraduate students to examine the relationship between frontal theta/beta ratio (TBR) and psychological symptoms assessed by the Symptom Checklist-90, finding that students with higher psychological symptom severity had significantly greater frontal theta and beta power and higher TBR, which positively correlated with total SCL-90 score and several symptom dimensions. Suggested that resting-state frontal TBR may serve as a potential neurophysiological correlate of mental health vulnerability in non-clinical populations.

papers.title: Repeated remimazolam sedation for interstitial brachytherapy in cervical cancer: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 100 cervical cancer patients undergoing repeated interstitial brachytherapy, remimazolam produced fewer intraoperative adverse events than propofol (17.78% vs 59.42%, RR 0.30, p<0.001), including lower respiratory depression and hypotension, with stable sedative requirements across three sessions and no differences in sleep quality.

papers.title: Haemodynamic and neurophysiological assessments for 2-year outcome prediction in neonates with hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy treated with therapeutic hypothermia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 37 studies (n=2721) found that abnormal amplitude-integrated EEG background at 36 hours reliably predicts adverse 2-year neurodevelopmental outcomes in neonates with hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy treated with therapeutic hypothermia (sensitivity 0.83, specificity 0.88, AUC 0.88), while cerebral near-infrared spectroscopy may offer complementary prognostic value and targeted neonatal echocardiography alone showed limited utility.

papers.title: Associations between preschool sleep consolidation trajectories and receptive vocabulary at age 5.
papers.summary: Using data from 1912 children in the Quebec Longitudinal Study of Child Development, this study identified three preschool sleep consolidation trajectories (rapid, typical, gradual) and found that children in the gradual trajectory had lower receptive vocabulary scores at age 5 compared with the typical trajectory (β=-0.10), with additional negative associations for immigrant mothers and certain childcare arrangements.

papers.title: Beyond Snoring, Sleepiness and Surgery: Update on the Prevalent Symptoms of and Treatment Effects in all Age Groups With Pediatric Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.summary: In a single-center cohort of 489 children with pediatric obstructive sleep apnea, restlessness, chronic insomnia, and kicking legs were more prevalent nocturnal symptoms than snoring, while neurocognitive issues affected 93.7% and improved more with positive airway pressure (94.9%) than with adenotonsillectomy (73.1%), with PAP showing threefold higher odds of neurocognitive improvement after adjustment.

papers.title: Sleep Disturbances and Sarcopenia in Older Adults: Clinical Associations, Potential Mechanisms, and Management Strategies.
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes observational evidence linking sleep disturbances (abnormal duration, poor quality, insomnia, circadian disruption, obstructive sleep apnea) to sarcopenia in older adults, discusses potential biological and behavioral mechanisms, and outlines management strategies, while highlighting that causality remains uncertain and prospective and randomized trials are needed.

papers.title: Patterns of screen use and their association with sleep among medical students: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: A cross-sectional questionnaire study of 1,063 Bulgarian and foreign medical students assessed screen time patterns and sleep characteristics. Greater screen time was weakly associated with later bedtime but only weakly and inconsistently with nocturnal sleep duration, while prolonged screen exposure and suboptimal sleep patterns were common.

papers.title: Concurrent observation and physical practice facilitates early closed motor skill learning: evidence from EEG source functional connectivity and behavioral performance.
papers.summary: This study compared motor observation (MO) alone versus concurrent observation and physical practice (MP) during early learning of 24-Style Tai Chi. MP produced stronger EEG source functional connectivity, better motor performance, and stronger positive brain-behavior correlations, supporting the AOT-NPT framework and the neurobehavioral advantage of combining physical practice with observation.

papers.title: Scn1a-mediated developmental regulation of prefrontal cortex plasticity and cognition.
papers.summary: This study induced Nav1.1 dysfunction in the adult medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) of mice to compare with adolescent effects. Adult dysfunction caused epileptic activity and depressive-like phenotypes but spared mPFC-dependent cognition and LTP, unlike adolescent dysfunction, revealing a developmental role for Nav1.1 in mPFC plasticity and cognition.

papers.title: Modulating stress and sleep through a multi-compound dietary supplement: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
papers.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
papers.summary: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial tested morning adaptogens, evening sleep supplements, and their combination in 103 healthy adults over two weeks. Morning ashwagandha and Rhodiola rosea supplementation improved perceived stress, subjective sleep quality, and positive affect compared to placebo, with minimal effects on other outcomes.

papers.title: The double-edged sword of rotational shift work: a qualitative study of worker perceptions in Saudi Arabia.
papers.summary: This qualitative phenomenological study examined how rotational shift work affects psychological well-being, work-life balance, and occupational outcomes among 16 petrochemical workers in Saudi Arabia. Three themes emerged: health effects (sleep disruption, circadian misalignment), complex work-life negotiations including religious obligations, and mixed occupational outcomes, extending the Job Demands-Resources framework to a non-Western context.

papers.title: Transdiagnostic patterns of electroencephalography (EEG)-derived aperiodic activity across schizophrenia-spectrum, bipolar, and depressive disorders: A systematic review.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesized 30 studies (N=2298) on EEG-derived aperiodic activity in schizophrenia-spectrum, bipolar, and depressive disorders, finding heterogeneous results in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders, more consistent flatter slopes and reduced offsets in major depressive and treatment-resistant depression, limited bipolar evidence, and sensitivity to treatment-related modulation. The authors conclude that aperiodic parameters may be more informative as context-sensitive within-subject markers of cortical state and treatment change than as fixed diagnostic signatures.

papers.title: Cognitive impairment in idiopathic intracranial hypertension: A conceptual framework and therapeutic implications.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on cognitive impairment in idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) and proposes a conceptual framework in which cognitive dysfunction arises from interactions among elevated intracranial pressure, cerebral venous hypertension, symptom amplifiers such as chronic headache, sleep disturbance, pulsatile tinnitus, and psychiatric comorbidity, and biological/socioeconomic modifiers. It argues that cognition should be recognized as a clinically meaningful and potentially treatment-responsive outcome in IIH, particularly in patients without papilledema.

papers.title: Comprehensive Health Predictors of Injury, Illness, and Separation From Service After Enrollment in Special Forces Assessment and Selection: A Two-Year Longitudinal Study.
papers.journal: Stress and health : journal of the International Society for the Investigation of Stress
papers.summary: In a two-year longitudinal study of 792 candidates entering U.S. Army Special Forces Assessment and Selection, baseline slower road march times were associated with 25–66% higher odds of injury, mental/behavioral illness, sleep disorder, and separation from service, whereas greater resistance training, better sleep quality, and higher protein intake were associated with 18–45% lower odds of injury. Elevated morning cortisol was associated with 23% lower odds of mental/behavioral illness, and negative mood, poorer sleep quality, and less social support were associated with 28–31% increased odds of separation.

papers.title: Explainable machine learning for identifying mild cognitive impairment in older adults with chronic diseases: Model development and temporal validation.
papers.summary: Using CHARLS data, this study developed and temporally validated an interpretable machine-learning model (prespecified XGBoost) to identify current mild cognitive impairment (MCI) in older adults with chronic diseases, achieving an AUROC of 0.692 in 2018 internal validation and 0.702 in 2020 temporal validation. TreeSHAP explanations were highly stable across survey waves (Spearman ρ = 0.996), with top predictors including number of living children, sleep duration, educational attainment, activities of daily living, and age.

papers.title: Sedentary accumulation patterns and mental health among university teachers: longitudinal evidence from a single-university two-wave cohort.
papers.summary: In a two-wave cohort of 769 university teachers, 12-month reductions in mean sitting-bout length and prolonged sitting (bouts ≥30 min) were associated with better WHO-5 well-being, lower perceived stress, and lower emotional exhaustion, but effect sizes were small (semi-partial f² < 0.02).

papers.title: Non-invasive preoperative prediction of surgical outcomes in drug-resistant epilepsy using seizure-related EEG network dynamics.
papers.summary: This study developed a non-invasive EEG source imaging framework to predict surgical outcomes in 50 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy undergoing SEEG-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation, using seizure-related brain network features from pre-ictal and ictal states. Features derived from the presumed epileptogenic zone achieved a maximum AUC of 0.936 and accuracy of 0.860, with SVM and logistic regression both performing competitively.

papers.title: A comparative study of traditional Chinese mind-body therapies on sleep quality, mental health, and quality of life in patients with sleep disorders: a network meta-analysis based on randomized controlled trials.
papers.summary: This network meta-analysis of 18 randomized controlled trials compared Tai Chi, Baduanjin, and Tai Chi combined with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TCCWTMS) for sleep quality, mental health, and quality of life in patients with sleep disorders. TCCWTMS was best for sleep quality (SMD = -1.15), only Tai Chi significantly improved mental health (SMD = 0.64), and both Tai Chi and Baduanjin significantly improved quality of life, with Baduanjin ranking highest.

papers.title: Chronic sleep deprivation promotes atherosclerosis via NFIL3/RORγt Axis mediated Th17/Treg imbalance, targeting IL-17A attenuates disease progression.
papers.summary: In LDL receptor-deficient mice, chronic sleep deprivation accelerated atherosclerosis and increased the Th17/Treg ratio by downregulating NFIL3 in CD4+ T cells, which derepressed RORγt; neutralizing IL-17A attenuated plaque progression and endothelial inflammation.

papers.title: How Virtual Reality and Relaxation Exercises Shape Pain, Sleep, Kinesiophobia and Anxiety Over Time After Impacted Third Molar Surgery?: A Randomized Controlled Study.
papers.summary: In a randomized trial of 36 patients after impacted third molar surgery, relaxation exercises alone or combined with virtual reality reduced pain (VAS) and anxiety (STAI-S) scores on postoperative days 2 and 7 compared to patient education alone.

papers.title: Effects of Perioperative Intranasal Dexmedetomidine Spray on Clinical Outcomes of Pulsed Radiofrequency in Patients with Zoster-Associated Pain: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized double-blind trial of 68 patients with zoster-associated pain undergoing pulsed radiofrequency, perioperative intranasal dexmedetomidine spray reduced hemodynamic fluctuations and improved postoperative pain and sleep quality scores compared to saline control, with no severe adverse events.

papers.title: Sleep quality, disturbance and the prevalence of obstructive sleep apnoea in chronic spontaneous urticaria and associated risk factors.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 327 adults with chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU), the prevalence of poor sleep quality was 59.3% (PSQI) and intermediate-to-high risk for obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) was 61.5% (STOP-Bang). Multivariable analysis identified symptomatic dermographism (OR 2.4) as a predictor of poor sleep quality, while female gender (OR 12.3), uncontrolled urticaria (OR 2.7), and dyslipidaemia (OR 3.1) were significant predictors for moderate-to-severe OSA risk.

papers.title: Association between night-shift frequency and metabolic syndrome among healthcare workers: a moderated mediation analysis of occupational stress and sleep quality.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 719 healthcare workers, ≥4 night shifts per month was associated with substantially higher odds of metabolic syndrome (OR 6.65), with an indirect association through occupational stress that was stronger at poorer sleep quality levels.

papers.title: Lifestyle-Driven Phenotypes in Sensitive Skin: A Cross-Sectional, Multicenter Study Across Urbanization Tiers.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional multicenter study of 151 women compared sensitive skin phenotypes across urbanization tiers using clinical, biophysical, and biomarker measures. In highly urbanized sensitive skin versus non-sensitive skin, prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) was 23.5% higher and protein carbonylation 17.9% higher; in the lifestyle comparison, highly urbanized living was associated with 185.0% higher PGE2, while moderately urbanized high-UV conditions were linked to 27.8% higher pigmentation and 27.3% elevated oxidative stress.

papers.title: Spiritual well-being, sleep quality as a buffer against burnout and in increasing professional fulfillment among healthcare professionals in the United Arab Emirates.
papers.journal: Journal of education and health promotion
papers.summary: A cross-sectional survey of 661 healthcare professionals in the UAE found that poor sleep quality and irregular circadian patterns were significantly associated with higher burnout, while higher spiritual well-being showed a strong negative correlation with burnout and a positive association with professional fulfillment. Multivariate analysis identified sleep regularity and spiritual well-being as significant independent predictors of both burnout and professional fulfillment.

papers.title: Effect of early regional anesthesia on postoperative cognitive function and the perioperative stress response in patients with hip fractures: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 76 elderly hip fracture patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty, administering anterior iliopsoas muscle space block (AIMSB) one day before surgery versus one hour before surgery did not significantly reduce the incidence of postoperative delirium (8.1% vs 12.8%; risk difference -4.7%; 95% CI [-18.4% to 9.0%]; P = 0.71). Transient early postoperative pain scores were lower in the day-before group at 6 hours, but differences did not survive multiple comparison correction, and an exploratory IL-6 curve AUC finding requires prospective validation.

papers.title: Cardiovascular health and depression among postpartum women in the United States.
papers.summary: Using cross-sectional NHANES 2007–2020 data from 7,208 reproductive-age women, this study examined the association between depression and cardiovascular health (CVH) by postpartum status. Postpartum women had significantly worse CVH scores for physical activity (48.7 vs 54.3) and BMI (57.3 vs 63.3) compared to non-postpartum women, and depression was associated with lower overall CVH; postpartum status modified the association only for sleep (p=0.005).

papers.title: Navigating the storm: A qualitative research on contributing factors to diabetes burnout in young adults with type 1 diabetes.
papers.journal: Journal of education and health promotion
papers.summary: This qualitative content analysis of semi-structured interviews with 11 young adults with type 1 diabetes in Iran identified four interrelated themes contributing to diabetes burnout: disruptions in self-management routines, external stressors and resource limitations, fluctuations in physical and emotional well-being, and the role of interpersonal and social support. These factors were exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, highlighting the need for holistic diabetes care addressing medical and psychosocial dimensions.

papers.title: Sleep disturbance, anxiety, and depression in postoperative ovarian cancer patients: prevalence, associated factors, and symptom interrelationships.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 302 postoperative ovarian cancer patients, sleep disturbance was the most prevalent psychological symptom (72.5%), followed by depression (40.1%) and anxiety (26.5%), with co-occurrence of all three in 18.2%. Depressive symptoms were independently associated with sleep disturbance, anxiety, and depression; recurrence and chemotherapy were associated with sleep disturbance; and cancer-related fatigue and family life satisfaction were associated with depressive symptoms.

papers.title: Study protocol for a randomized controlled trial comparing penetrating needling and cognitive behavioral therapy for subjective tinnitus.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a randomized controlled trial to evaluate penetrating needling versus cognitive behavioral therapy for subjective tinnitus in 72 participants, with primary outcomes including the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory and Tinnitus Questionnaire.

papers.title: Correction: Toward clinical translation of TMS-EEG: an integrative review of multidimensional neurophysiological measures.
papers.summary: This is a correction notice for a previously published article on the clinical translation of TMS-EEG; it does not present new findings or a scientific study.

papers.title: Correction: Foreground, midground, and restoration: EEG and preference responses to depth-controlled rural scenes.
papers.summary: This is a correction notice for a previously published article on EEG and preference responses to depth-controlled rural scenes; it does not present new findings or a scientific study.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
